answer: I'd like to talk about something I hope to own in the next few years. A vehicle I would love to own one day is a reliable, fuel-efficient car, ideally something practical rather than flashy. I'm thinking of a small family car with enough room for my parents and my younger sister. Even in a modest town like Sirajganj, having my own car would make daily life significantly more [[convenient]]. The main reason I want one is the freedom it offers; I would no longer depend on crowded public transport or unreliable schedules. At the moment, getting anywhere means haggling with rickshaw drivers or squeezing onto packed buses, especially on the long journey to Dhaka. I imagine using it for my daily commute and for weekend trips out of town, which I rarely manage now. Above all, I'd use it to drive my parents to my grandparents' village home, which we visit often, and to see my elder sister and her children in Dhaka whenever we like. What appeals to me most is the sense of [[independence]] it would bring. I would probably choose something environmentally friendly, since fuel efficiency matters to me. Owning a car would feel like a real [[milestone]], a sign of stability and progress. I think my father, who worked so hard for so many years, would be especially proud to sit in the passenger seat. Honestly, though it is a considerable expense, I think it would genuinely improve my quality of life. It is a goal I am steadily working towards, and I know the sense of freedom would make it thoroughly [[worthwhile]].

followUps.q: Can you drive at the moment?
followUps.answer: Not very well, honestly. I've had a few lessons from a cousin, but I'd need proper training before driving on our roads, because traffic can be quite [[unpredictable]], especially on the highways.

followUps.q: Would you prefer an electric car?
followUps.answer: Ideally, yes, because it would be better for the environment. But charging points are still rare outside the big cities here, so for now a fuel-efficient car seems far more realistic.

note: Persona fix: 'busy city' changed to Sirajganj as a modest town; added family trips to the village and Dhaka and his father's pride.
